title: M101 Unit 8 · Accumulation and the fundamental theorem
rows: \(\Delta x=(b-a)/n\). Left samples \(a+i\Delta x\), i=0,…,n−1; right samples i=1,…,n. Multiply every height by its width.
\(\int_a^b f(x)\,dx=\lim\sum f(c_i)\Delta x_i\) as the largest width tends to zero. Continuous f on [a,b] guarantees existence.
\(\int_b^a f=-\int_a^b f\); \(\int_a^a f=0\); \(\int_a^b f=\int_a^c f+\int_c^b f\).
\(\int_a^b(\alpha f+\beta g)=\alpha\int_a^b f+\beta\int_a^b g\), for constants α,β.
Net signed total; units = integrand units × input units. For a<b and m≤f≤M: \(m(b-a)\leq\int_a^b f\leq M(b-a)\).
\(A(x)=\int_a^x f(t)\,dt\) gives \(A\prime(x)=f(x)\) at interior x when f is continuous. A(a)=0.
\(\frac{d}{dx}\int_a^{g(x)}f(t)\,dt=f(g(x))g\prime(x)\). Continuous f, differentiable g. A moving lower limit contributes a minus sign.
\(\int_a^b f(x)\,dx=F(b)-F(a)\), if f is continuous and F′=f on the interval.
\(\int f(x)\,dx=F(x)+C\). Equal derivatives imply a constant difference on an interval; constants cancel in endpoint subtraction.

\(x^p\mapsto\frac{x^{p+1}}{p+1}\) (p≠−1); \(1/x\mapsto\ln|x|\); \(e^x\mapsto e^x\); \(\cos x\mapsto\sin x\); \(\sin x\mapsto-\cos x\). Valid real intervals; reciprocal excludes zero; trig uses radians.
Differentiate an antiderivative; substitute initial data; inspect the whole domain, signs, units and bounds. Benchmark code against a hand sum and an exact integral.
code:
def left_sum(f, a, b, n):
    # Increasing interval; positive integer n.
    width = (b - a) / n
    total = 0.0
    for i in range(n):
        total += f(a + i * width) * width
    return total
